subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in procD.lm: not read my variable

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in procD.lm: not read my variable
parts:
Mateus,

you definitely need to build a geomorph dataframe, and specifically point to the corresponding object within the procD.lm command through the "data=" argument. Please make sure to carefully read the help files of both functions, and follow the instructions into detail, also making sure to use the same variable names for building the geomorph.data.frame and when writing the formula to be tested through procD.lm.

Good luck!

Antigoni

On 10/03/2020 22:42, Mateus Cruz Loss wrote:
Hy everyone, 

I have a weird problem:

Wen I run my Procrustes Anova, the comand procD.lm not read my independent variable in data frame.

Code:
> anova_forma_d <-procD.lm(alinhamento_coords_d~df_forma_d $ CE) 

#alinhamento_coords_d= coordinates of  my 2d data contained in an 2d array.
#df_forma_d= my data.frame with my independent variable: CE (5 age groups: I:V). This data are original from a .csv table.

Result (error):
Preliminary Model Fit...  0%
Error in eval(attr(terms(var.exp), "variables"), data, parent.frame()) : object 'CE' not found.

... Old analyzes that were working when redone also stopped working.
... I tried use geomorph.data.frame, uninstall and install RStudio and R, excludes the user preferences, restore my Windows and none alternatives work it.
... The names of column in data.frame and in code are same.

Thanks a lot!
--

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in procD.lm: not read my variable
parts:
Hi Antigoni, 

Thanks for answer! 
I solved the problem changing the factor of my independt variable, using: > factor() >as.numeric().
Same using gemorph.data.frame, was necessary change the factor. I do not understand error caused, but at the moment it is resolved.

Certainly was a big help!
Thank you very much!
